questions.text: Which of the following setup procedures is best suited for separating a mixture of two miscible liquids with close boiling points?
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation uses a fractionating column to separate miscible liquids whose boiling points are close (less than 25°C apart). Simple distillation is used when boiling points differ significantly.

questions.text: The mass number of an element is 27 and its atomic number is 13. How many neutrons are in the nucleus of this atom?
questions.explanation: Number of neutrons = Mass number - Atomic number = 27 - 13 = 14.

questions.text: What type of chemical bond exists between sodium and chlorine in sodium chloride (NaCl)?
questions.explanation: Sodium transfers its single valence electron to chlorine, forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions. The electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions forms an ionic (electrovalent) bond.

questions.text: Which of the following electronic configurations represents an alkali metal?
questions.explanation: Alkali metals (Group 1 elements) have a single electron in their outermost s-orbital (ns¹). 1s²2s²2p⁶3s¹ corresponds to Sodium (Na).

questions.text: According to Charles's Law, the volume of a given mass of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature at constant:
questions.explanation: Charles's Law states that V ∝ T at constant pressure (P).

questions.text: Calculate the molar mass of hydrated copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI), CuSO₄·5H₂O. [Cu=63.5, S=32, O=16, H=1]
Which of the following gas law equations represents the Ideal Gas Equation?
questions.explanation: The Ideal Gas Equation combines Boyle's, Charles's, and Avogadro's laws into PV = nRT, where n is the number of moles and R is the universal gas constant.

questions.text: The phenomenon whereby an element exists in two or more forms in the same physical state is called:
questions.explanation: Allotropy is the existence of an element in two or more different structural forms in the same physical state (e.g., Diamond and Graphite for carbon).

questions.text: Which of the following substances is an allotrope of carbon that conducts electricity?
questions.explanation: In graphite, each carbon atom uses only 3 of its 4 valence electrons for bonding, leaving delocalized free electrons that conduct electricity.

questions.text: The catalyst used in the Haber process for the industrial manufacture of ammonia is:
questions.explanation: The Haber process (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃) uses finely divided iron as a catalyst to speed up the reaction at lower temperatures.

questions.text: What is the pH of a neutral solution at 25°C?
questions.explanation: At 25°C, pure water has equal concentrations of H⁺ and OH⁻ ions (1 × 10⁻⁷ M), giving a pH of -log(1 × 10⁻⁷) = 7.

questions.text: A solution that resists a change in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added is called a:
questions.explanation: Buffer solutions contain a weak acid and its conjugate base (or a weak base and its conjugate acid) to maintain a relatively stable pH.

questions.text: Oxidation can be defined as the:
questions.explanation: Remember the mnemonic OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss of electrons, Reduction Is Gain of electrons.

questions.text: What is the oxidation number of manganese in potassium permanganate (KMnO₄)?
questions.explanation: Let x be oxidation state of Mn: (+1) + x + 4(-2) = 0 → 1 + x - 8 = 0 → x = +7.

questions.text: The electrode where oxidation occurs in an electrochemical cell is the:
questions.explanation: Oxidation always occurs at the Anode (An Ox), while reduction occurs at the Cathode (Red Cat).

questions.text: Which of the following metals is extracted industrially by the electrolysis of its molten chloride?
questions.explanation: Sodium is highly reactive and cannot be reduced by chemical agents like carbon. It is extracted via electrolysis of molten NaCl in a Downs cell.

questions.text: An endothermic reaction is one in which heat energy is:
questions.explanation: Endothermic processes absorb heat energy from their surroundings (ΔH > 0), causing the temperature of the surroundings to drop.

questions.text: What is the IUPAC name for CH₃CH₂CH₂OH?
questions.explanation: It is a 3-carbon chain (propan-) with an alcohol functional group (-OH) attached to carbon 1, making it propan-1-ol.

questions.text: Hydrocarbons containing at least one carbon-carbon double bond (C=C) belong to the family of:
questions.explanation: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing one or more double bonds with general formula CₙH₂ₙ.

questions.text: The structural functional group present in alkanoic acids is:
questions.explanation: The carboxyl group (-COOH) is the defining functional group of organic carboxylic acids (alkanoic acids).

questions.text: Vegetable oils are converted into solid fats (margarine) by the process of:
questions.explanation: Hydrogenation adds hydrogen gas across double bonds in liquid unsaturated vegetable oils using a nickel catalyst to turn them into saturated solid fats.

questions.text: The functional group responsible for the characteristic sweet smell of alkanoates (esters) is:
questions.explanation: Esters have the ester linkage (-COO- or -COOR), which gives flowers and fruits their sweet fragrances.

questions.text: Which gas is liberated when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with calcium carbonate?
questions.explanation: Acids react with carbonates to produce salt, water, and carbon dioxide gas: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂↑.

questions.text: What type of salt is formed when a dibasic acid is partially neutralized by a base?
questions.explanation: Partial neutralization leaves replaceable hydrogen atoms in the salt (e.g., NaHSO₄), producing an acid salt.

questions.text: The universal indicator turns red in a solution with a pH of:
questions.explanation: Universal indicator turns red/pink in strongly acidic conditions (pH 1-3). Neutral is green, and alkaline is blue/purple.

questions.text: Which separation technique is suitable for obtaining pure water from sea water?
questions.explanation: Distillation boils seawater to vaporize pure water and then condenses it back to liquid, leaving dissolved salts behind. Evaporation recovers salt, not pure water.

questions.text: The shape of a water molecule (H₂O) is:
questions.explanation: Water has 2 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs of electrons around the central oxygen atom. Lone pair repulsion pushes the bonds into a bent/V-shaped geometry (~104.5°).

questions.text: Which halogen exists as a liquid at room temperature and pressure?
questions.explanation: Bromine (Br₂) is the only non-metallic element that is a dark red liquid at standard conditions. F₂ and Cl₂ are gases; I₂ is solid.

questions.text: Periodic trend indicates that atomic radius generally decreases across a period due to:
questions.explanation: Across a period, protons are added to the nucleus while electrons fill the same main energy level. Higher positive nuclear charge pulls the electrons closer, reducing radius.

questions.text: Temporary hardness of water is caused by the presence of dissolved:
questions.explanation: Hydrogencarbonates of calcium and magnesium (Ca(HCO₃)₂ / Mg(HCO₃)₂) cause temporary hardness. Sulfates and chlorides cause permanent hardness.

questions.text: Temporary hardness in water can be removed by:
questions.explanation: Boiling decomposes soluble hydrogencarbonates into insoluble carbonates precipitate: Ca(HCO₃)₂ → CaCO₃↓ + H₂O + CO₂.

questions.text: Which of the following pollutants is primarily responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer?
questions.explanation: UV light releases chlorine radicals from CFCs in the stratosphere, which break down ozone (O₃) molecules into oxygen (O₂).

questions.text: The raw materials used in the manufacture of soap during saponification are fats/oils and:
questions.explanation: Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of fats/oils (triglycerides) using concentrated caustic alkali like NaOH or KOH.

questions.text: Which gas turns lime water milky?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide reacts with lime water (Ca(OH)₂) to form an insoluble white precipitate of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃).

questions.text: The process of heating sulfide ores strongly in the presence of excess air is known as:
questions.explanation: Roasting converts metal sulfides into metal oxides and sulphur dioxide gas by heating in excess air. Calcination heats ores in limited air.

questions.text: An element X has atomic number 12 and element Y has atomic number 17. The formula of the compound formed between them is:
questions.explanation: Element X (2,8,2) loses 2 electrons to form X²⁺. Element Y (2,8,7) gains 1 electron to form Y⁻. Balancing charges gives XY₂.

questions.text: Which of the following is an intensive property of matter?
questions.explanation: Intensive properties do not depend on the amount of matter present (e.g., density, boiling point). Mass and volume are extensive properties.

questions.text: Activation energy is best defined as the minimum energy required to:
questions.explanation: Activation energy (E_a) is the minimum kinetic energy reacting particles must possess for collisions to successfully yield products.

questions.text: In a reversible reaction at equilibrium, adding a positive catalyst will:
options: Shift the equilibrium position to the right
Speed up both forward and reverse reactions equally
Decrease the rate of reverse reaction
questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy equally for both forward and reverse reactions, so it speeds up the rate of reaching equilibrium without altering the position or product yield.

questions.text: Methane reacts with chlorine in the presence of ultraviolet light via which mechanism?
questions.explanation: UV light splits Cl₂ homolytically into free chlorine radicals (Cl•), initiating a photochemical free radical substitution mechanism with alkanes.

questions.text: Which of the following hydrocarbons will decolorize bromine water in the dark?
questions.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons like ethene undergo rapid electrophilic addition reactions with aqueous bromine in the dark, turning brown bromine water colorless.

questions.text: What product is formed at the anode during the electrolysis of concentrated sodium chloride solution (brine) using inert carbon electrodes?
questions.explanation: In concentrated NaCl, chloride ions (Cl⁻) are at a much higher concentration than hydroxide ions (OH⁻), so Cl⁻ is preferentially discharged at the anode to produce Cl₂ gas.

questions.text: Faraday's first law of electrolysis states that the mass (m) of a substance liberated at an electrode is directly proportional to the:
questions.explanation: Faraday's 1st Law: m ∝ Q → m = ZQ = ZIt, where Q is electric charge in Coulombs (I × t).

questions.text: Calculate the volume occupied by 0.5 moles of an ideal gas at STP. [Molar volume at STP = 22.4 dm³/mol]
questions.explanation: Volume = Moles × Molar volume = 0.5 mol × 22.4 dm³/mol = 11.2 dm³.

questions.text: Which of the following standard conditions defines STP?
questions.explanation: Standard Temperature and Pressure (STP) is defined as 0°C (273 K) and 1 atm (760 mmHg or 101.3 kPa).

questions.text: What type of oxide is zinc oxide (ZnO)?
questions.explanation: Amphoteric oxides (like ZnO, Al₂O₃, PbO) react with both acids and strong bases to produce salt and water.

questions.text: Which oxide listed below is a neutral oxide?
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide (CO), water (H₂O), and dinitrogen monoxide (N₂O) are neutral oxides—they react with neither acids nor bases.

questions.text: The standard heat of combustion (ΔH_c°) of a substance is always:
questions.explanation: Combustion reactions release heat energy to the surroundings (exothermic process), so their enthalpy change (ΔH) is always negative.

questions.text: Which acid is present in human gastric juice aiding digestion?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is secreted by parietal cells in the stomach wall, creating the acidic environment (pH 1.5-3.5) required for pepsin digestion.

questions.text: What is the principal ore from which aluminum is extracted?
questions.explanation: Bauxite (Al₂O₃·2H₂O) is the chief commercial ore of aluminum. Haematite is iron ore; Galena is lead ore.

questions.text: Which of the following setup procedures is best suited for purifying an impure solid sample like copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI)?
questions.explanation: Crystallization is used to purify soluble salts/solids from impurities by dissolving the impure sample in hot solvent and cooling it to form pure crystals. Sublimation is only for solids that vaporize directly (like iodine or ammonium chloride).

questions.text: An element X has two isotopes: ³⁵X with a relative abundance of 75% and ³⁷X with an abundance of 25%. What is the relative atomic mass of X?
questions.explanation: RAM = (35 × 75/100) + (37 × 25/100) = 26.25 + 9.25 = 35.5. This corresponds to chlorine (³⁵⁵Cl).

questions.text: Which of the following chemical species contains dative (coordinate) covalent bonding?
questions.explanation: In the ammonium ion (NH₄⁺), nitrogen shares a lone pair of electrons with a hydrogen ion (H⁺) that has no electrons of its own, forming a dative covalent bond alongside three normal covalent bonds.

questions.text: Which element in the periodic table has the highest electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Fluorine lies at the top-right of Group 7 (Halogens) and is the most electronegative element with a Pauling value of 4.0. Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group.

questions.text: A gas occupies 500 cm³ at 27°C. What volume will it occupy at 127°C if the pressure remains constant?
questions.explanation: Convert to Kelvin: T₁ = 27 + 273 = 300 K, T₂ = 127 + 273 = 400 K. Using Charles's Law: V₂ = V₁ × T₂/T₁ = 500 × 400/300 = 666.7 cm³.

questions.text: What mass of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is required to prepare 250 cm³ of a 0.2 mol/dm³ solution? [Na=23, O=16, H=1]
questions.explanation: Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g/mol. Volume in dm³ = 250/1000 = 0.25 dm³. Moles = 0.2 × 0.25 = 0.05 mol. Mass = 0.05 × 40 = 2.0 g.

questions.text: According to Graham's Law of Diffusion, the rate of diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its:
questions.explanation: Graham's Law states that R ∝ 1/√d (or 1/√M), where d is gas density and M is molar mass, at constant temperature and pressure.

questions.text: Which of the following forms of carbon is amorphous?
questions.explanation: Charcoal, lampblack, and coke are non-crystalline (amorphous) forms of carbon. Diamond, graphite, and fullerenes have well-defined crystalline structures.

questions.text: What is the geometry of a molecule of methane (CH₄)?
questions.explanation: Carbon in methane undergoes sp³ hybridization with 4 bonding electron pairs mutually repelling to the corners of a regular tetrahedron with bond angles of 109.5°.

questions.text: Industrial production of nitric acid (HNO₃) from ammonia by catalytic oxidation is known as the:
questions.explanation: The Ostwald process oxidizes NH₃ over platinum-rhodium catalyst to produce NO, which is further oxidized and absorbed in water to yield HNO₃.

questions.text: Calculate the pH of a 0.001 mol/dm³ solution of hydrochloric acid (HCl).
questions.explanation: HCl is a strong monobasic acid, so [H⁺] = 0.001 M = 10⁻³ M. pH = -log[H⁺] = -log(10⁻³) = 3.

questions.text: Which indicator is most suitable for titrating a strong acid against a weak base?
questions.explanation: Strong acid vs. weak base equivalence point occurs in the acidic range (pH 3-5). Methyl orange changes color between pH 3.1–4.4, making it the ideal indicator.

questions.text: During a redox reaction, an oxidizing agent is a substance that:
questions.explanation: An oxidizing agent causes another species to lose electrons by accepting/gaining those electrons itself; in the process, its own oxidation number decreases (it gets reduced).

questions.text: What is the oxidation number of sulfur in the thiosulfate ion (S₂O₃²⁻)?
questions.explanation: Let x be the average oxidation number of sulfur: 2x + 3(-2) = -2 → 2x - 6 = -2 → 2x = +4 → x = +2.

questions.text: In a galvanic (voltaic) cell, the negative electrode is the:
questions.explanation: In galvanic cells generating electrical energy from spontaneous reactions, the anode loses electrons (oxidation) and serves as the negative terminal. (Note: in electrolytic cells, the anode is positive).

questions.text: How many Coulombs of electricity are passed when a current of 2.5 A flows for 2 hours?
The enthalpy change (ΔH) for an exothermic reaction is:
questions.explanation: Exothermic reactions release heat energy to surroundings, meaning products have lower enthalpy than reactants (H_products - H_reactants < 0).

questions.text: What is the IUPAC name for CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃?
questions.explanation: The longest continuous carbon chain has 4 carbons (butane). A methyl group (-CH₃) is attached to carbon 2. Thus, 2-methylbutane.

questions.text: Hydrocarbons containing carbon-carbon triple bonds (-C≡C-) are called:
questions.explanation: Alkynes are unsaturated acyclic hydrocarbons with general formula CₙH₂ₙ⁻₂ containing triple bonds.

questions.text: Alkanols react with alkanoic acids in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄ to form:
questions.explanation: Esterification reaction: R-COOH + R'-OH → R-COO-R' + H₂O.

questions.text: The conversion of glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide by yeast enzymes is called:
questions.explanation: Enzymatic breakdown of sugars (like glucose) by zymase in yeast under anaerobic conditions produces ethanol and CO₂: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂.

questions.text: Which functional group turns blue litmus paper red and liberates CO₂ gas with NaHCO₃?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids (-COOH) are acidic enough to react with sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃) giving effervescence of CO₂ gas.

questions.text: Which gas is responsible for the rotten egg smell in qualitative salt analysis?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) is a colorless gas with a characteristic offensive odor of rotten eggs.

questions.text: Which of the following salts is insoluble in water at room temperature?
questions.explanation: All nitrates, Group 1 metal salts, and ammonium salts are soluble. Most sulfates are soluble except PbSO₄, BaSO₄, and CaSO₄ (sparingly).

questions.text: Methyl orange indicator turns which color in an alkaline solution?
questions.explanation: Methyl orange is red in acidic media (pH < 3.1), orange at transition, and yellow in neutral/alkaline media (pH > 4.4).

questions.text: Which technique separates components of black ink dyes based on their differential solubility and adsorption?
questions.explanation: Paper chromatography separates soluble pigments as a mobile phase solvent carries components along a stationary cellulose paper phase at different rates.

questions.text: The bond angle in a perfectly tetrahedral molecule like methane (CH₄) is:
questions.explanation: Symmetric four-coordinate sp³ tetrahedral geometry maximizes distance between electron pairs at 109.5°.

questions.text: Which non-metal is a good conductor of heat and electricity?
questions.explanation: Graphite is a non-metallic allotrope of carbon featuring hexagonal layers with delocalized π-electrons free to move and conduct current along planes.

questions.text: Ionization energy generally increases across a period from left to right because:
options: Nuclear charge increases and atomic radius decreases
questions.explanation: Higher effective nuclear charge pulling electrons closer across a period makes valence electrons harder to remove, thus raising first ionization energy.

questions.text: Permanent hardness in water is caused by dissolved:
questions.explanation: Soluble sulfates or chlorides of calcium and magnesium (CaSO₄, MgSO₄, CaCl₂) cause permanent hardness, which cannot be removed by simple boiling.

questions.text: Permanent hardness of water can be removed by treating water with:
questions.explanation: Sodium carbonate precipitates soluble calcium and magnesium ions as insoluble carbonates: CaSO₄(aq) + Na₂CO₃(aq) → CaCO₃(s)↓ + Na₂SO₄(aq).

questions.text: Which greenhouse gas is released in large quantities from cattle farming and rice paddies?
questions.explanation: Anaerobic fermentation by methanogenic bacteria in livestock digestion and flooded paddy field soils produces significant atmospheric methane (CH₄).

questions.text: The major constituent of natural gas is:
questions.explanation: Natural gas consists primarily of methane (CH₄), typically making up 80% - 95% of its composition.

questions.text: Which gas forms a brown ring during the test for nitrate ions (NO₃⁻)?
questions.explanation: In the brown ring test, conc. H₂SO₄ and fresh FeSO₄ reduce nitrate to nitric oxide (NO), which reacts with unoxidized Fe²⁺ to form the nitrosyl-iron complex ring.

questions.text: Iron is extracted from haematite (Fe₂O₃) in a blast furnace using which reducing agent?
questions.explanation: Inside the blast furnace at elevated temperatures, carbon monoxide (CO) acts as the primary reducing agent: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.

questions.text: Element A (atomic number 11) and Element B (atomic number 8) combine. The empirical formula of the product is:
questions.explanation: Atomic number 11 is Sodium (1s²2s²2p⁶3s¹ → A⁺). Atomic number 8 is Oxygen (1s²2s²2p⁴ → B²⁻). Combining charges yields A₂B (Na₂O).

questions.text: A reaction is spontaneous at all temperatures if:
questions.explanation: Gibbs Free Energy equation: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS. For spontaneity, ΔG must be negative. When ΔH is negative (exothermic) and ΔS is positive (entropy increase), ΔG is guaranteed negative at all temperatures.

questions.text: Increasing the total pressure on the equilibrium mixture N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) will:
questions.explanation: According to Le Chatelier's principle, an increase in pressure shifts equilibrium toward the side with fewer gas moles. Reactants = 4 moles gas; Products = 2 moles gas. Thus, it shifts right.

questions.text: Which mechanism occurs when propene reacts with hydrogen bromide (HBr)?
questions.explanation: The electron-rich double bond (C=C) in propene attacks the electrophilic H⁺ from HBr, proceeding via Markovnikov electrophilic addition.

questions.text: Addition of aqueous silver nitrate (AgNO₃) followed by dilute nitric acid to a solution gives a white precipitate soluble in aqueous ammonia. The anion present is:
questions.explanation: Chloride ions (Cl⁻) precipitate as white silver chloride (AgCl), which dissolves readily in dilute ammonia. (Bromide gives cream ppt soluble in conc. NH₃; Iodide gives yellow ppt insoluble in NH₃).

questions.text: How many structural isomers exist for butane (C₄H₁₀)?
questions.explanation: Butane has 2 structural isomers: straight-chain n-butane (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃) and branched 2-methylpropane / isobutane (CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃).

questions.text: The mass of copper deposited when 2.0 A passes through CuSO₄ solution for 9650 seconds is: [Cu=63.5, 1 F=96500 C]
questions.explanation: Reduction: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu(s) (2 Faradays deposit 1 mole Cu). Q = I × t = 2 × 9650 = 19300 C. 19300/96500 = 0.2 Faradays. Since Cu²⁺ needs 2 F/mol, 0.2 F deposits 0.1 mol. 0.1 × 63.5 = 6.35 g.

questions.text: A real gas deviates most from ideal gas behavior under which conditions?
questions.explanation: At low temperature (particles lose kinetic energy and intermolecular forces become significant) and high pressure (gas volume shrinks so molecular volume is no longer negligible), real gases deviate heavily from ideal behavior.

questions.text: The molecular formula of a compound with empirical formula CH₂O and molar mass 60 g/mol is: [C=12, H=1, O=16]
questions.explanation: Empirical formula mass = 12 + 2(1) + 16 = 30 g/mol. n = 60/30 = 2. Molecular formula = (CH₂O)₂ = C₂H₄O₂.

questions.text: What product is formed at the cathode during electrolysis of dilute sulphuric acid using platinum electrodes?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen ions (H⁺) migrate to the cathode, gain electrons, and are reduced to form hydrogen gas: 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂(g).

questions.text: Which compound exhibits optical isomerism (chirality)?
questions.explanation: Lactic acid contains a chiral carbon atom bonded to four different groups (-H, -OH, -CH₃, -COOH), enabling non-superimposable mirror image enantiomers.

questions.text: Catalytic cracking of heavy petroleum fractions is primarily used to increase the yield of:
questions.explanation: Cracking breaks down long-chain alkane hydrocarbons into shorter, higher-demand fuels—principally petrol/gasoline and alkenes for chemical industries.

questions.text: The functional group present in aldehydes is:
questions.explanation: Aldehydes contain a terminal carbonyl group (-CHO). Ketones contain a non-terminal carbonyl group (-CO-).

questions.text: Hydrolysis of sucrose yields an equimolar mixture of:
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide made of glucose and fructose bonded together. Acid or enzymatic (invertase) hydrolysis splits sucrose into glucose + fructose ('invert sugar').

questions.text: The change in state from solid directly to gas without passing through liquid is:
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct phase transition from solid to gas phase (e.g., dry ice, iodine crystals, ammonium chloride, camphor).

questions.text: Which of the following gas samples diffuses fastest under the same conditions of temperature and pressure? [H=1, C=12, N=14, O=16, S=32]
questions.explanation: By Graham's Law, the rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass. Molar masses: CH₄ = 16, NH₃ = 17, CO₂ = 44, SO₂ = 64. Methane (CH₄) has the lowest molar mass, so it diffuses fastest.

questions.text: What volume of 0.5 mol/dm³ H₂SO₄ is required to neutralize completely 25.0 cm³ of 1.0 mol/dm³ NaOH?
questions.explanation: Balanced equation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O (n_a = 1, n_b = 2). Using C_aV_a/C_bV_b = n_a/n_b: (0.5 × V_a)/(1.0 × 25) = 1/2 → 0.5V_a = 12.5 → V_a = 25.0 cm³.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of gases cannot be collected over water?
questions.explanation: Gases that are extremely soluble in water (like HCl and NH₃) dissolve instantly instead of displacing water, so they cannot be collected over water.

questions.text: What is the conjugate base of HSO₄⁻?
questions.explanation: A conjugate base is formed when a species loses a proton (H⁺). HSO₄⁻ - H⁺ = SO₄²⁻.

questions.text: Which transition metal ion is colored in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ has an incomplete d-subshell (3d⁹), allowing d-d electron transitions that produce a blue color. Zn²⁺ (3d¹⁰) and Sc³⁺ (3d⁰) have empty or full d-orbitals, rendering them colorless.

questions.text: The industrial process for manufacturing tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is called the:
questions.explanation: The Contact process oxidizes SO₂ to SO₃ using a vanadium(V) oxide (V₂O₅) catalyst, which is then absorbed in concentrated acid to yield H₂SO₄.

questions.text: Which of the following structural formulas represents an ester?
questions.explanation: Esters contain the carboxylate ester group (-COO-). CH₃COOCH₃ is methyl ethanoate. Option A is a ketone, C is an ether, and D is an aldehyde.

questions.text: Which element exhibits diagonal relationship with Beryllium (Be) in the Periodic Table?
questions.explanation: Beryllium (Be) and Aluminum (Al) share a diagonal relationship due to similar charge-to-radius ratios, giving both metals amphoteric oxides and similar chemical properties.

questions.text: What is the hybridization state of the central carbon atom in ethyne (C₂H₂)?
questions.explanation: In ethyne (H-C≡C-H), each carbon forms two σ-bonds (one C-H and one C-C) and two π-bonds, which corresponds to sp hybridization and linear geometry (180°).

questions.text: How many unpaired electrons are in the ground state configuration of a gaseous nitrogen atom (N, Z=7)?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen's configuration is 1s² 2s² 2pₓ¹ 2pₕ¹ 2pₖ¹. By Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity, the three electrons in the 2p subshell remain unpaired in separate orbitals.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds will give a white precipitate with Fehling's or Tollens' reagent?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes (like ethanal) act as reducing agents and reduce Tollens' reagent (Ag⁺) to silver metal (a silver mirror/precipitate) and Fehling's reagent (Cu²⁺) to red Cu₂O. Ketones do not react.

questions.text: The term 'entropy' refers to the measure of a system's:
questions.explanation: Entropy (S) quantifies molecular disorder or chaos in a system. Gases have higher entropy than liquids, which have higher entropy than solids.

questions.text: What is the effect of adding a non-volatile solute to a solvent?
options: Raises boiling point and lowers freezing point
Lowers boiling point and raises freezing point
Lowers both boiling point and freezing point
Raises both boiling point and freezing point
questions.explanation: Dissolving a non-volatile solute lowers vapor pressure, resulting in boiling point elevation and freezing point depression.

questions.text: Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen in urea, CO(NH₂)₂. [C=12, O=16, N=14, H=1]
Which halogen is strongest as an oxidizing agent?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest standard reduction potential and highest electronegativity among the halogens, making it the most powerful oxidizing agent.

questions.text: Which of the following standard enthalpy changes is always negative?
questions.explanation: Neutralization between an acid and a base is strictly exothermic (ΔH < 0), releasing heat as H⁺ and OH⁻ combine to form water.

questions.text: Electrolysis of dilute copper(II) sulfate solution using copper electrodes leads to:
options: Dissolution of copper anode into solution
questions.explanation: When reactive copper electrodes are used, the anode oxidizes (Cu(s) → Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻), causing the copper anode to dissolve into the solution.

questions.text: What product is formed when propene reacts with water in the presence of dilute acid (H₂SO₄)?
questions.explanation: Acid-catalyzed hydration of propene follows Markovnikov's rule: the hydrogen atom adds to the carbon with more hydrogen atoms (CH₂), placing the -OH group on carbon 2 to give propan-2-ol.

questions.text: A solution has a hydrogen ion concentration [H⁺] = 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol/dm³. What is its pH? [log 2 = 0.30]
Which element is extracted commercially by the Solvay process?
questions.explanation: The Solvay process manufactures sodium carbonate (washing soda) from brine (NaCl), ammonia (NH₃), and limestone (CaCO₃).

questions.text: What volume of gas is evolved at STP when 10.0 g of calcium carbonate decomposes completely on heating? [Ca=40, C=12, O=16, Molar volume at STP=22.4 dm³/mol]
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Molar mass of CaCO₃ = 40 + 12 + 48 = 100 g/mol. Moles of CaCO₃ = 10.0/100 = 0.10 mol. Volume of CO₂ = 0.10 × 22.4 = 2.24 dm³.

questions.text: Which gas turns acidified potassium dichromate(VI) solution from orange to green?
questions.explanation: Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) acts as a reducing agent and reduces orange dichromate ions (Cr₂O₇²⁻) to green chromium(III) ions (Cr³⁺).

questions.text: Which property of transition metals accounts for their ability to form complex ions?
questions.explanation: Transition metals have vacant d-orbitals and high nuclear charge density, allowing them to accept electron pairs donated by ligands to form coordinate complex ions.

questions.text: What type of polymer is nylon-6,6?
questions.explanation: Nylon-6,6 is synthesized via condensation polymerization between hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid, linking monomers through amide linkages (-CONH-) with elimination of water.

questions.text: The general formula for the homologous series of alkanals is:
questions.explanation: Alkanals (aldehydes) contain one double bond (C=O) and have the general formula CₙH₂ₙO (e.g., ethanal C₂H₄O).

questions.text: What mass of copper will be deposited by passing 5.0 A of current through Cu²⁺ solution for 30 minutes? [Cu=64, 1 F=96500 C]
Which of the following separation techniques relies on differences in density?
questions.explanation: Centrifugation spins mixtures at high speed to separate suspended particles based on density (denser solids settle to the bottom quickly).

questions.text: What is the order of reaction if doubling the concentration of reactant A quadruples the rate of reaction?
questions.explanation: Rate = k[A]ⁿ. If [2A]ⁿ = 4 → 2ⁿ = 4 → n = 2. The reaction is second order with respect to A.

questions.text: The oxide of an element dissolves in water to turn red litmus paper blue. The oxide is likely:
questions.explanation: Metallic oxides like sodium oxide (Na₂O) are basic. They dissolve in water to produce strong alkalis (NaOH) that turn red litmus blue. Non-metal oxides are acidic.

questions.text: How many σ (sigma) and π (pi) bonds are present in a molecule of benzene (C₆H₆)?
questions.explanation: Benzene has 6 C-H σ-bonds, 6 C-C σ-bonds, and 3 delocalized π-bonds across the ring, giving a total of 12σ and 3π bonds.

questions.text: Which radioisotope is used in carbon dating to determine the age of organic artifacts?
questions.explanation: Carbon-14 (¹⁴C) is a beta-emitting radioactive isotope with a half-life of ~5730 years, used to date biological artifacts up to ~50,000 years old.

questions.text: Water gas is a gaseous mixture of:
questions.explanation: Water gas is produced by passing steam over red-hot coke (C + H₂O → CO + H₂). Producer gas is CO + N₂.

questions.text: Which of the following oxides shows both acidic and basic properties?
questions.explanation: Aluminum oxide (Al₂O₃) is amphoteric—it reacts with acids (forming aluminum salts) and strong alkalis (forming aluminates).

questions.text: Which gas is produced at the anode during the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride?
questions.explanation: In molten NaCl, chloride ions (Cl⁻) migrate to the positive anode and undergo oxidation: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂(g) + 2e⁻.

questions.text: What is the empirical formula of a compound containing 40.0% Carbon, 6.7% Hydrogen, and 53.3% Oxygen? [C=12, H=1, O=16]
questions.explanation: Moles: C = 40.0/12 = 3.33, H = 6.7/1 = 6.7, O = 53.3/16 = 3.33. Divide by smallest (3.33): C=1, H=2, O=1. Empirical formula = CH₂O.

questions.text: Which metal can displace hydrogen from cold water?
questions.explanation: Very reactive metals (Group 1 and Group 2 like Na, K, Ca) react vigorously with cold water to release hydrogen gas: Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂↑.

questions.text: Which statement is correct regarding an endothermic reaction?
options: Enthalpy of products is greater than enthalpy of reactants
questions.explanation: Endothermic reactions absorb heat, meaning energy is taken in, so products store more enthalpy than reactants (H_products > H_reactants, making ΔH > 0).

questions.text: How many moles of solute are contained in 500 cm³ of a 2.0 mol/dm³ H₂SO₄ solution?
questions.explanation: Volume in dm³ = 500/1000 = 0.5 dm³. Moles = C × V = 2.0 × 0.5 = 1.0 mol.

questions.text: Which functional group is detected using 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNPH)?
questions.explanation: 2,4-DNPH reacts with carbonyl compounds (both aldehydes and ketones) to form yellow/orange/red hydrazone precipitates.

questions.text: Which gas is responsible for global warming (greenhouse effect) in highest atmospheric volume?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) accounts for the vast majority of human-driven greenhouse gas emission volume, trapping thermal infrared radiation.

questions.text: The shape of an ammonia molecule (NH₃) is:
questions.explanation: Nitrogen in NH₃ has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair of electrons. Lone pair repulsion squeezes the H-N-H bond angle to 107°, giving a trigonal pyramidal shape.

questions.text: Pure gold is referred to as 24 carats. What percentage of pure gold is present in 18-carat gold?
Which law states that equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules?
questions.explanation: Avogadro's Law states that V ∝ n at constant temperature and pressure.

questions.text: Addition of dilute hydrochloric acid to an unknown solid produces effervescence. The gas turned lime water milky. The solid contains:
questions.explanation: Carbonates (CO₃²⁻) and hydrogencarbonates (HCO₃⁻) react with acids to liberate CO₂ gas, which forms insoluble white CaCO₃ in lime water.

questions.text: What is the functional group of primary alkanols?
options: -OH attached to a carbon atom bonded to at least two hydrogen atoms
-OH attached to a carbon atom bonded to three alkyl groups
questions.explanation: Primary alcohols (R-CH₂-OH) have their -OH attached to a carbon carrying two or three hydrogens (e.g., methanol, ethanol).

questions.text: Which process removes permanent hardness from water by exchange of ions?
questions.explanation: Permutit (sodium aluminum silicate) replaces calcium and magnesium ions (Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺) in hard water with sodium ions (Na⁺).

questions.text: Which element has the ground-state electronic configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴?
questions.explanation: Sum of electrons = 2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 4 = 16, which corresponds to Sulfur (S).

questions.text: The standard heat of formation (ΔH_f°) of an element in its standard state is:
questions.explanation: By thermodynamic convention, the standard enthalpy of formation of any pure element in its most stable physical state at 298 K and 1 atm is zero.

questions.text: What type of reaction occurs when ethanol is converted to ethene using concentrated H₂SO₄ at 170°C?
questions.explanation: Concentrated H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent at 170°C, removing a molecule of water from ethanol to yield ethene (C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O).

questions.text: Which alloy consists primarily of copper and zinc?
questions.explanation: Brass is an alloy of Copper and Zinc. Bronze is an alloy of Copper and Tin.

questions.text: What is the oxidation number of sulfur in tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid (H₂SO₄)?
questions.explanation: Let x be the oxidation number of sulfur: 2(+1) + x + 4(-2) = 0 → 2 + x - 8 = 0 → x = +6.

questions.text: Which of the following physical or chemical processes is endothermic?
options: Dissolution of ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl) in water
questions.explanation: Dissolving NH₄Cl in water absorbs heat energy from the surroundings (ΔH > 0), causing the container temperature to drop. Freezing, condensation, and combustion are exothermic.

questions.text: What is the pH of a solution with a hydrogen ion concentration [H⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol/dm³?
What is the IUPAC name for CH₃CH₂OH?
questions.explanation: A 2-carbon alkane chain with an -OH functional group is named ethanol.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds belongs to the alkyne homologous series?
questions.explanation: Alkynes follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ⁻₂. For n = 2, the formula is C₂H₂ (ethyne).

questions.text: What is the principal ore used in the industrial extraction of aluminum?
questions.explanation: Bauxite (Al₂O₃ · 2H₂O) is the primary commercial ore of aluminum.

questions.text: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element on the periodic table due to its small atomic radius and high effective nuclear charge.

questions.text: Calculate the molar mass of anhydrous sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃). [Na=23, C=12, O=16]
Which gas turns lime water (Ca(OH)₂) milky?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide reacts with lime water to produce an insoluble white precipitate of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃).

questions.text: A positive catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction by:
options: Increasing the volume of the reaction vessel
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy (E_a), allowing a higher fraction of molecular collisions to be successful.

questions.text: What is the empirical formula of a compound that contains 80% Carbon and 20% Hydrogen by mass? [C=12, H=1]
questions.explanation: Moles of C = 80/12 = 6.67. Moles of H = 20/1 = 20. Divide by 6.67: C = 1, H = 20/6.67 ≈ 3. Empirical formula is CH₃.

questions.text: Which of the following noble gases is used in filling weather balloons?
questions.explanation: Helium is non-flammable and extremely light (second lightest element), making it safe for weather balloons.

questions.text: The functional group present in alkanals (aldehydes) is:
questions.explanation: -CHO is the terminal carbonyl group characteristic of aldehydes.

questions.text: What type of bond is formed when two atoms share a pair of electrons equally?
questions.explanation: Equal sharing of electrons between atoms of identical or very similar electronegativity forms a non-polar covalent bond.

questions.text: The process of separating crude oil into its various fractions based on boiling points is called:
questions.explanation: Petroleum is separated into gasoline, kerosene, diesel, and other fractions via fractional distillation in a tall fractionating tower.

questions.text: What is the oxidation state of chromium in potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇)?
Which of the following aqueous solutions will have a pH greater than 7?
questions.explanation: Sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) is a salt formed from a strong base (NaOH) and a weak acid (H₂CO₃). Its aqueous solution hydrolyzes to give a basic solution (pH > 7).

questions.text: According to Le Chatelier's principle, what happens when temperature is increased in an exothermic reversible reaction?
questions.explanation: Heat is treated as a product in an exothermic reaction. Increasing temperature adds heat, so the system shifts to the left (endothermic direction) to absorb the excess heat.

questions.text: What volume of 0.1 mol/dm³ HCl is required to completely neutralize 20.0 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ Na₂CO₃?
questions.explanation: Reaction: 2HCl + Na₂CO₃ → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ (n_a = 2, n_b = 1). C_aV_a/C_bV_b = n_a/n_b → (0.1 × V_a)/(0.1 × 20) = 2/1 → V_a = 40.0 cm³.

questions.text: Which gas is liberated when concentrated trioxonitrate(V) acid (HNO₃) reacts with copper metal?
questions.explanation: Concentrated HNO₃ is a strong oxidizing agent. It reacts with copper metal to give dense reddish-brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide (NO₂).

questions.text: The loss of water of crystallization from a hydrated salt when exposed to atmosphere is termed:
questions.explanation: Efflorescence is the spontaneous loss of water of crystallization by hydrated salts when their vapor pressure is greater than that of the surrounding air.

questions.text: What is the total number of atoms present in one molecule of copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) pentahydrate (CuSO₄ · 5H₂O)?
questions.explanation: CuSO₄: 1 Cu + 1 S + 4 O = 6 atoms. 5H₂O: 5 × (2 H + 1 O) = 15 atoms. Total = 6 + 15 = 21 atoms.

questions.text: Which element is present in all organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Carbon is the fundamental structural element present in every organic molecule.

questions.text: Which process is used to separate a mixture of two immiscible liquids like kerosene and water?
questions.explanation: A separating funnel separates immiscible liquids based on their density differences (the denser water settles at the bottom and is drained off first).

questions.text: The law of definite proportions states that:
options: Matter can neither be created nor destroyed
Equal volumes of gases contain equal numbers of molecules
A pure chemical compound always contains the same elements combined in the same fixed proportion by mass
Gases react in simple whole-number ratios by volume
questions.explanation: Formulated by Joseph Proust, this law states that a given chemical compound always contains its component elements in fixed ratio by mass, regardless of source.

questions.text: What is the shape of a carbon dioxide (CO₂) molecule?
questions.explanation: CO₂ has two double bonds (O=C=O) and no lone pairs on the central carbon atom, resulting in a linear molecular shape with a 180° bond angle.

questions.text: Electrovalent (ionic) compounds typically possess:
questions.explanation: Ionic compounds have strong electrostatic forces holding their giant 3D crystal lattices together, requiring significant heat energy to melt or boil.

questions.text: What is the formula of the precipitate formed when aqueous barium chloride (BaCl₂) is added to dilute sodium tetraoxosulphate(VI) (Na₂SO₄)?
questions.explanation: Barium sulphate (BaSO₄) is an insoluble white precipitate formed in the ionic double displacement reaction: Ba²⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq) → BaSO₄(s)↓.

questions.text: Which halogen is a dark purple/black solid at room temperature that sublimes upon heating to form purple vapor?
questions.explanation: Iodine (I₂) is a dark crystalline solid that sublimes directly into a violet gas when heated gently.

questions.text: Chlorine gas acts as a bleaching agent in the presence of water because it produces:
questions.explanation: Cl₂ + H₂O ⇌ HCl + HOCl. Hypochlorous acid (HOCl) releases atomic oxygen ([O]) which oxidizes dyes to render them colorless.

questions.text: What mass of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is contained in 1.0 dm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ NaOH solution? [Na=23, O=16, H=1]
questions.explanation: Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g/mol. Mass = C × V × M = 0.1 × 1.0 × 40 = 4.0 g.

questions.text: Which of the following organic compounds decolorizes acidified potassium tetraoxomanganate(VII) (KMnO₄)?
questions.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons like ethene undergo oxidation with acidified KMnO₄, converting purple MnO₄⁻ ions to colorless Mn²⁺ ions (Baeyer's test).

questions.text: Polymers that soften when heated and can be remolded repeatedly are called:
questions.explanation: Thermoplastics (e.g., polythene, PVC) lack cross-links between polymer chains, allowing them to melt and be reshaped upon heating.

questions.text: What is the conjugate acid of the ammonia molecule (NH₃)?
questions.explanation: A conjugate acid is formed when a base accepts a proton (H⁺): NH₃ + H⁺ → NH₄⁺.

questions.text: In an electrochemical cell, reduction always takes place at the:
questions.explanation: Reduction (gain of electrons) always occurs at the Cathode in both galvanic and electrolytic cells.

questions.text: What is the standard temperature and pressure (STP) volume of 1 mole of any ideal gas?
questions.explanation: By Avogadro's hypothesis, 1 mole of any gas at STP (273 K, 1 atm) occupies 22.4 dm³ (or 22400 cm³).

questions.text: Which metal is added to iron to make stainless steel resistant to rusting?
questions.explanation: Stainless steel contains iron alloyed with chromium (at least 10.5%) and nickel, forming a protective passive oxide film that prevents corrosion.

questions.text: Which method is used to collect gases that are less dense than air and insoluble in water?
questions.explanation: Collecting over water works for any gas that is insoluble/sparingly soluble in water, regardless of density.

questions.text: Hydrolysis of starch yields which simple monosaccharide unit?
questions.explanation: Starch is a polysaccharide composed of long chains of α-glucose monomers linked by glycosidic bonds. Complete hydrolysis breaks it down into glucose.

questions.text: What product is formed when ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄?
questions.explanation: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. The product is the sweet-smelling ester ethyl ethanoate.

questions.text: The Brownian motion observed in colloidal suspensions is caused by:
options: Unbalanced collisions between colloidal particles and solvent molecules
questions.explanation: Brownian motion is the continuous random zig-zag motion of colloidal particles resulting from impacts by fast-moving molecules of the dispersion medium.

questions.text: What is the pH of a neutral solution at 25°C?
questions.explanation: At 25°C, pure neutral water has [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ M, yielding a pH of 7.

questions.text: Which of the following gas pollutants is colorless, odorless, highly toxic, and binds strongly to hemoglobin in blood?
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide (CO) binds with hemoglobin to form carboxyhemoglobin with an affinity ~200 times higher than oxygen, preventing oxygen transport.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of electrons that can occupy an s-subshell?
questions.explanation: An s-subshell consists of 1 orbital, which holds a maximum of 2 electrons with opposite spins (Pauli Exclusion Principle).

questions.text: Which of the following salt solutions forms a gelatinous white precipitate with NaOH that dissolves in excess NaOH?
questions.explanation: Zn²⁺ forms white amphoteric Zn(OH)₂ precipitate with NaOH, which dissolves in excess NaOH to form a clear sodium tetrahydroxozincate(II) complex solution [Zn(OH)₄]²⁻.

questions.text: Standard conditions for measuring gas molar volumes are:
questions.explanation: Standard Temperature and Pressure (STP) is defined as 0°C (273.15 K) and 1 atm (101.3 kPa).

questions.text: The process of converting solid coal into gaseous fuel by heating in limited air is called:
questions.explanation: Coal gasification reacts coal with steam and oxygen at high temperatures to produce synthesis gas (CO + H₂).

questions.text: Which element belongs to Group 17 (Halogens) and Period 3 of the Periodic Table?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is in Period 2; Chlorine is in Period 3; Bromine is in Period 4; Iodine is in Period 5.

questions.text: What mass of water is produced when 4.0 g of hydrogen gas reacts completely with excess oxygen gas? [H=1, O=16]
questions.explanation: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. 4 g H₂ = 4/2 = 2.0 moles of H₂. From stoichiometry, 2.0 moles of H₂ produces 2.0 moles of H₂O. Mass = 2.0 × 18 = 36.0 g.

questions.text: What type of reaction is represented by CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl?
questions.explanation: A hydrogen atom in methane is replaced/substituted by a chlorine atom in a free-radical substitution mechanism initiated by UV light.

questions.text: Which of the following subatomic particles determines the atomic number of an element?
questions.explanation: The atomic number (Z) of an atom is defined strictly as the number of protons in its nucleus.

questions.text: What volume will 0.5 moles of nitrogen gas occupy at STP? [Molar volume of gas at STP = 22.4 dm³]
questions.explanation: Volume = number of moles × 22.4 dm³ = 0.5 × 22.4 = 11.2 dm³.

questions.text: Which of the following separation techniques is best suited for obtaining pure water from sea water?
questions.explanation: Simple distillation boils off water leaving the salt behind, then condenses the steam back into pure liquid water. Evaporation leaves the salt but loses the water.

questions.text: Atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers are called:
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, leading to different mass numbers.

questions.text: Which gas is evolved when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with calcium carbonate?
questions.explanation: Acid + Metal Carbonate → Salt + Water + Carbon dioxide gas (CO₂).

questions.text: The process by which a solid changes directly into a gas without passing through the liquid state is called:
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct phase transition from solid to gas (e.g., ammonium chloride, iodine, camphor).

questions.text: Which of the following oxides is amphoteric?
questions.explanation: Zinc oxide (ZnO) reacts with both acids and bases to form salts, making it amphoteric. Other common examples are Al₂O₃ and PbO.

questions.text: What is the concentrated form of trioxonitrate(V) acid called when it acts as a strong oxidizing agent?
questions.explanation: Concentrated HNO₃ readily gives off nascent oxygen, making it a powerful oxidizing agent that can oxidize non-metals like sulfur and carbon.

questions.text: The arrangement of elements in the modern Periodic Table is based on their:
questions.explanation: The modern periodic law states that physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

questions.text: Which type of chemical bond is present in a molecule of hydrogen gas (H₂)?
questions.explanation: Two hydrogen atoms share one pair of electrons equally to form a single non-polar covalent bond (H-H).

questions.text: What is the pH of a 0.001 mol/dm³ solution of hydrochloric acid (HCl)?
Which of the following metals reacts vigorously with cold water to liberate hydrogen gas?
questions.explanation: Sodium is a highly reactive Group 1 alkali metal that reacts violently with cold water to produce NaOH and H₂ gas.

questions.text: The continuous movement of solvent particles through a semi-permeable membrane from a dilute to a concentrated solution is called:
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the selective movement of solvent molecules across a semi-permeable membrane toward higher solute concentration.

questions.text: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: Ethane (C₂H₆) contains only single carbon-carbon bonds, making it an alkane (saturated).

questions.text: The formula CₙH₂ₙ represents which homologous series?
questions.explanation: Alkenes contain one double bond (C=C) and follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ.

questions.text: How many moles of solute are present in 250 cm³ of a 2.0 mol/dm³ solution?
questions.explanation: V = 250/1000 = 0.25 dm³. Moles = Concentration × Volume = 2.0 × 0.25 = 0.50 moles.

questions.text: A substance that absorbs moisture from the atmosphere without forming a solution is described as:
questions.explanation: Hygroscopic substances absorb water vapor from the air but stay solid (or liquid if already liquid, like conc. H₂SO₄). Deliquescent substances absorb so much water that they dissolve into a liquid solution.

questions.text: The catalyst used in the industrial preparation of ammonia by the Haber process is:
questions.explanation: Finely divided iron with an alumina promoter is used as a catalyst in the Haber process (N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃).

questions.text: What is the product formed when hydrogen gas is passed over heated copper(II) oxide?
questions.explanation: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O. Hydrogen reduces copper(II) oxide to reddish-brown copper metal while being oxidized to water.

questions.text: Which element has the electronic configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴?
questions.explanation: Total electrons = 2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 4 = 16. Element 16 on the periodic table is Sulfur (S).

questions.text: An indicator that turns pink in basic solution and colorless in acidic solution is:
questions.explanation: Phenolphthalein is clear in neutral and acidic solutions (pH < 8.3) and turns bright pink in alkaline solutions.

questions.text: The process of burning a substance in the presence of excess oxygen is called:
questions.explanation: Combustion is a high-temperature exothermic chemical reaction between a fuel and an oxidant (usually atmospheric oxygen).

questions.text: What is the valence of nitrogen in ammonia (NH₃)?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen forms 3 covalent bonds with 3 hydrogen atoms in NH₃, giving it a valency of 3.

questions.text: Which of the following is a physical change?
questions.explanation: Melting of ice is a reversible state transition (H₂O(s) → H₂O(l)) with no new chemical substance formed.

questions.text: Which law states that the total pressure exerted by a mixture of non-reacting gases is equal to the sum of their partial pressures?
questions.explanation: Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures states P_total = P₁ + P₂ + P₃ + ... for non-reacting gas mixtures.

questions.text: What mass of oxygen gas (O₂) is contained in 0.25 moles? [O=16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass of O₂ = 16 × 2 = 32 g/mol. Mass = 0.25 × 32 = 8.0 g.

questions.text: The phenomenon whereby an element exists in two or more different physical forms in the same state is known as:
questions.explanation: Allotropy is the ability of an element (like Carbon: diamond, graphite; or Sulfur: rhombic, monoclinic) to exist in multiple structural forms in the same physical state.

questions.text: Which gas is responsible for the characteristic smell of rotten eggs?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) is a poisonous gas recognized by its distinct smell of rotten eggs.

questions.text: What type of reaction takes place when an acid reacts with a base to form salt and water?
questions.explanation: Neutralization is the reaction between H⁺ ions from an acid and OH⁻ ions from a base to form neutral H₂O and a salt.

questions.text: Which organic product is formed from the fermentation of glucose using yeast?
questions.explanation: Yeast secretes the enzyme zymase, which converts glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂.

questions.text: What is the major constituent of natural gas?
questions.explanation: Natural gas consists mostly of methane (CH₄), usually making up 70% to 90% of the mixture.

questions.text: Which particle has a mass of approximately 1 atomic mass unit (amu) and carries no electrical charge?
questions.explanation: A neutron resides in the atomic nucleus with a relative mass of 1 and a neutral charge (0).

questions.text: The gas law that describes the relationship between gas volume and absolute temperature at constant pressure is:
questions.explanation: Charles's Law states that at constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature (V ∝ T).

questions.text: What is the oxidation state of hydrogen in sodium hydride (NaH)?
questions.explanation: Sodium is a metal with oxidation state +1. In ionic metal hydrides, hydrogen acts as a hydride ion (H⁻) with an oxidation state of -1.

questions.text: Which metal is extracted commercially by the electrolysis of its molten chloride or oxide?
questions.explanation: Highly reactive metals like Aluminium, Sodium, and Calcium are extracted using electrolysis because chemical reducing agents like carbon are not strong enough.

questions.text: What volume of carbon dioxide at STP is produced when 10 g of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) is decomposed by heat? [Ca=40, C=12, O=16, Molar volume=22.4 dm³]
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Molar mass of CaCO₃ = 100 g/mol. Moles = 10/100 = 0.1 mol. Volume = 0.1 × 22.4 = 2.24 dm³.

questions.text: Which halogen is a reddish-brown liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Bromine (Br₂) is the only non-metallic element that exists as a volatile reddish-brown liquid at room temperature.

questions.text: The addition of a small amount of acid or base to a buffer solution causes:
questions.explanation: A buffer solution resists changes in pH when small quantities of acid or base are added.

questions.text: An element in Group 2 of the Periodic Table will form an ion with a charge of:
questions.explanation: Group 2 alkaline earth metals have 2 valence electrons which they lose to achieve a noble gas configuration, forming 2+ cations (e.g., Mg²⁺, Ca²⁺).

questions.text: What mass of water is required to prepare a 0.5 molal solution using 1 mole of solute?
questions.explanation: Molality = moles of solute / mass of solvent in kg → 0.5 = 1/mass → mass = 2.0 kg.

questions.text: Chemical equilibrium is reached in a reversible reaction when:
options: The concentration of reactants equals products
The rate of forward reaction equals the rate of reverse reaction
All reactants are completely used up
questions.explanation: Dynamic chemical equilibrium occurs when the forward and reverse reactions happen at identical rates, keeping reactant and product concentrations constant over time.

questions.text: Which instrument is used to measure the relative atomic mass of elements accurately?
questions.explanation: A mass spectrometer separates isotopes based on mass-to-charge ratios (m/z) to determine isotopic abundances and precise relative atomic masses.

questions.text: The drying agent commonly used to dry ammonia gas is:
questions.explanation: Ammonia is basic, so it reacts with acidic drying agents (conc. H₂SO₄, P₄O₁₀) and forms a complex with CaCl₂. Quicklime (CaO) is basic, making it safe to dry NH₃.

questions.text: What is the molecular shape of methane (CH₄)?

questions.text: Saponification is the chemical process used in the manufacture of:
questions.explanation: Saponification is the alkaline hydrolysis of fats or oils (esters) with caustic soda (NaOH) or potash (KOH) to yield soap and glycerol.

The hardness of temporary hard water is caused by the presence of dissolved:
questions.explanation: Temporary hardness is caused by dissolved hydrogen carbonates of calcium and magnesium (Ca(HCO₃)₂ or Mg(HCO₃)₂), which can be removed simply by boiling.

questions.text: Which alloy is composed of copper and zinc?
questions.explanation: Brass is an alloy made of copper and zinc. (Bronze is copper and tin).

questions.text: Which of the following statements is true regarding a catalyst?
options: It changes the enthalpy change (ΔH) of the reaction
It gets consumed during the reaction
It alters the path of the reaction to lower activation energy
It shifts the position of equilibrium
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds up reaction rates without being consumed or changing ΔH or equilibrium yield; it only lowers the activation energy barrier.

questions.text: How many unpaired electrons are in an atom of oxygen in its ground state? (Atomic number = 8)
questions.explanation: Electron configuration of Oxygen (Z=8): 1s² 2s² 2p⁴. Following Hund's rule, the 2p subshell has 1 orbital with paired electrons and 2 orbitals with 1 unpaired electron each. Total = 2 unpaired electrons.
